reason: Four narrow project skills serve one class: the Metaform web map and chat page. Folding them into one umbrella with labeled sections; their detail moves to references/ and the depth probe moves to scripts/.

The mascot ask path computed the clicked-element line at delivery time, so a click while the system agent started changed or dropped the reference. The chat path fixed it at queue time; the fix moves the mascot path to match.
The page parts are ES modules and the trace checked them with `node --input-type=module --check` (ok). The queued-path test technique was needed to make a waiting step run at all.

Two copies of the same hit-test drifted (nodeAt3d wider than the hover check), so one click both opened the ask field and recorded a neighbouring node. The shared-predicate rule is the fix the trace verified.

The chat page's view-context handling changed in ticket graphical#12e (take at send, give back on failure). The skill's chat section had no rule for this, and a future sender would reintroduce consume-before-success or drop-after-ok, both of which the episode showed to be wrong.

The "Still open" race in the view-context section was fixed in 43e00e6b/4a4ceb7d-era work: the direct send now marks CLICKED.told before the post and undoes it on failure. The stale line would send the next session to re-investigate a closed race.

The episode found that a mascot question waiting on the chat box's failed system-agent call stayed unsent without notice. The skill's ask-path guidance never said a failed send must release waiting asks, so the next session could reproduce the same gap.

Commit e021bccc set a rule the skill does not yet state: the click is told only when it reaches the system agent, and a message to another agent must leave it untold. Without it the next session may mark the click told on every send.
A browser test on the mascot click needed a layout swap that is not written anywhere; the next test author will lose time debugging a silent miss.

The episode rebuilt word bubbles from planes/canvas to SVG in one layer with a new tail rule and click path; the web-map skill is the one a future session edits this with, and it had no bubble guidance. Rule is durable and class-level (the page's figure/bubble drawing).

The episode fixed a stale-read race: a read begun before a redraw landed after it and overwrote the newer state (drawHelpdesk, then the same guard in renderAgents). The numbered-draw guard is a reusable web-map rule, and no existing section covers out-of-order page reads.

The episode built a new-page project rule and an FQC reviewer found the first version (folder mtimes) wrong. The rule is a durable pitfall for any future change to which project the web page opens on, and this skill is the one loaded for page work.

Episode fixed a real defect: leaveStage removed seat meshes from the scene, so returning to a running table showed no figures. The fix and its test step are not recorded in the skill, and the next stage edit could reintroduce it.

Agent hover labels and names were added to the page in this episode, and the page's contract for them (one reused element, text set on change, shared option words) is not in this skill. The scratch-instance browser check and its cleanup were the verification path and are worth keeping for the next page change.
Absorbs metaform-web-board and metaform-web-gui-hang-diagnosis: all three are the Metaform web page. The broadened description covers the board and freeze triggers the absorbed skills carried.

Adds two labelled subsections from the absorbed board and hang-diagnosis skills. The board section states the current card behaviour (whole top line draggable, click opens the ticket). The stale 2026-10-19 card snapshot is not carried, since it contradicts that current behaviour.
Keeps the web umbrella's index trigger inside the 60-character budget. The board and freeze triggers are carried by the subsections below it.
Removes a stray backslash the earlier board patch wrote before its quoted phrase; the quote is the person's phrase and reads plainly now.
Removes a stray backslash before a quoted phrase in the hang-diagnosis subsection.

The live server runs the main checkout, so a worktree's page change can only be verified by routing page files from the worktree in a read-only headless probe; the evidence the probe produced is the reusable pattern.

The figure-click and held-message contract was built and verified this episode, and no existing skill states the single click path, the held-chat rule or the native-subagent routing. A future page edit would otherwise add a second click path or a per-map copy, which the new code already removed.

Ticket code.system.management.knowledge#76 lost a side column to a global aside rule that no test caught; the screenshot showed it. The rule is a web-page layout trap that the next panel change will hit again.

A ticket about chat references was delivered in this episode. The reference-link behaviour, hex item numbers, %23 encoding and the restart-needed rule are not in the web-map skill yet, and a future change to chat refs would otherwise re-derive them. The restart line reconciles the "restart only with agreement" rule with the restart that happened here.

The seahorse mascot vanished while page tests passed. The cause was a live server started before commit 3b40e763 added the task_name field the page reads, so the page drew nothing and raised no error. The triage section named stale servers but gave no check for a missing field in a live row, and no note that a restart needs the person's yes.

The episode checked a live-page fix with a headless probe that aborted writes. That method (abort non-GET, read endpoint, screenshot, count page errors) is reusable and the skill only covers scratch-instance runs.

The read-only probe section lets a fix be checked on the live page before restart, but it does not say how. The episode confirmed a fix this way by answering the endpoint with the missing field in the probe.
